newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian coal futures market seen closer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian coal futures market seen closer.

text.p: The prospect of an open market in coal trading was getting closer ever day, an energy consultant to the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) said on Thursday.

The main lever for this was occurring through pressure by Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) and the Japanese consumer for lower power prices, Julian Fairfield told Reuters at the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) Outlook conference.
The SFE would have to wait for the development of an openly-available market-basis price before it could introduce coal futures trading, he said.
The present pricing system raised the cost of production of coal through weakening price signals, he told the conference.
This increased labour union power and allowed "lame duck" producers to continue to operate, he said.
It also prevented the opening of large-scale low-cost mines which could reduce operating costs in some cases to A$6.00-A$12.00 a tonne from A$20.00-A$30.00 a tonne he said.
